an8.9:1.1: “Monks, speaking rightly of Nanda, one could say, ‘He is a son of a good family.’
an8.9:1.2: Speaking rightly of Nanda, one could say, ‘He is strong.’
an8.9:1.3: Speaking rightly of Nanda, one could say, ‘He is handsome.’
an8.9:1.4: Speaking rightly of Nanda, one could say, ‘He is fiercely passionate.’
an8.9:1.5: If Nanda did not guard the doors of his senses, did not know moderation in eating, was not devoted to wakefulness, and was not endowed with mindfulness & alertness, how would he be able to follow the holy life, perfect & pure?
an8.9:1.6: “This is Nanda’s guarding of the doors of his senses:
an8.9:1.7: If he should look to the east, he looks focusing his entire awareness, (thinking,)
an8.9:1.8: ‘As I am looking thus to the east, greed & distress, evil unskillful qualities, will not flow out.’
an8.9:1.9: That’s how he is alert there.
an8.9:2.1: If he should look to the west…
an8.9:2.6: to the intermediate directions, he looks focusing his entire awareness, (thinking,)
an8.9:2.7: ‘As I am looking thus to the intermediate directions, greed & distress, evil unskillful qualities, will not flow out.’
an8.9:2.8: That’s how he is alert there.
an8.9:2.9: This is Nanda’s guarding of the doors of his senses.
an8.9:3.1: “This is Nanda’s knowledge of moderation in eating:
an8.9:3.2: Nanda takes his food reflecting appropriately,
an8.9:3.3: not playfully, nor for intoxication, nor for putting on bulk, nor for beautification, but simply for the survival & continuance of this body, for ending its afflictions, for the support of the holy life, (thinking,) ‘I will destroy old feelings (of hunger) & not create new feelings (from overeating). Thus I will maintain myself, be blameless, & live in comfort.’
an8.9:3.4: This is Nanda’s knowledge of moderation in eating.
an8.9:4.2: There is the case where Nanda during the day, sitting & pacing back & forth, cleanses his mind of any qualities that would hold the mind in check.
an8.9:4.3: During the first watch of the night [dusk to 10 p.m.], sitting & pacing back & forth, he cleanses his mind of any qualities that would hold the mind in check.
an8.9:4.4: During the second watch of the night [10 p.m. to 2 a.m.], reclining on his right side, he takes up the lion’s posture, one foot placed on top of the other, mindful, alert, with his mind set on getting up [either as soon as he awakens or at a particular time].
an8.9:4.5: During the last watch of the night [2 a.m. to dawn], sitting & pacing back & forth, he cleanses his mind of any qualities that would hold the mind in check.
an8.9:4.6: This is Nanda’s devotion to wakefulness.
an8.9:5.1: “This is Nanda’s being in mindfulness & alertness:
an8.9:5.2: There is the case where feelings are known to Nanda as they arise, known as they persist, known as they subside.
an8.9:5.3: Perceptions are known as they arise, known as they persist, known as they subside.
an8.9:5.4: Thoughts are known as they arise, known as they persist, known as they subside.
an8.9:5.5: This is Nanda’s being in mindfulness & alertness.
an8.9:6.1: “Monks, if Nanda did not guard the doors of his senses, did not know moderation in eating, was not devoted to wakefulness, and was not endowed with mindfulness & alertness, how would he be able to follow the holy life, perfect & pure?”
